title: Scalable High-Density Sensor-to-Memory Architectures: Topology, Automated Ingestion, and In-Memory Bitwise State Processing
summary: This monograph is written for a specific engineering objective: to use the architecture it describes as a platform for in-memory processing, that is, for building and continuously operating on a very large live state dataset (up to 10,616,832 nodes) that resides entirely in on-chip SRAM. On the real-time path the dataset is never written to disk, flash, or a database, and it is updated and evaluated with in-place bitwise operations rather than record-oriented I/O.
